3. That, the present respondent No.1 instituted Other Suit No. 76 of 2000 and also filed Pre-emption Case No. 43 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Ghatail, Tangail, one for declaration that the alleged Ewaznama deed No. 483 dated 18.1.2000 executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.1 and registered with the Office of the Sub Registrar, Ghatail, Tangail, is actually a deed of sale and the other one for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of the self same property, respectively. It is stated that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 without disclosing anything to the plaintiff/petitioner, very secretly created a deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 showing TK. 17,000/- as the value of the suit land and got the same registered in the Sub Registry Office. Thereafter, the defendant No.2 sold .34 acre of land from the schedule of the said exchange deed to defendant No.1 by a so-called sale deed dated 23.5.2000 at a consideration of taka 10,5000/- for the same, meaning that the defendant No.1 got back the same by the said so-called sale deed. In fact, there was no transaction of consideration money and no handing over of possession of the land in question. The price of both the exchanged and sold land always remained the same. It is stated that the plaintiff came to know about the aforesaid two deeds on 15.7.2000 when the defendant No.2 went to hand over possession of the land in question to defendant No.1 and thereafter, on 26.7.2000 upon obtaining the certified copy of the alleged deed. Thus he instituted the suit. 

 4. In the pre-emption petition the present respondent No.1 stated that the case land measuring .67 acre, along with other lands in plot Nos. 88, 86 and 87 of Mouza-Bhadrabari, PS. Ghatail, Tangail, originally belonged to Abdul Gani Siddique and his wife, Somedonnessa. That on the death of Abdul Gani Siddique his wife Somedonnessa became the owner and possessor of the aforesaid land. Her two sons, namely, Abdus Sattar and Abdul Majid having died earlier, Somedonnessa distributed her entire properties between her living sons, daughter and grandson and granddaughter by a registered wasiatnama dated 7.4.1960 pursuant to which her son Abdul Latif, Monir Uddin, daughter Rowshanara, grandson (the plaintiff/pre-emptor) and his other brother and sister got their saham in the suit property. Defendant Opposite Party No.2 and his brother (sons of predeceased Abdul Majid) became the owners and possessor of the suit land by dint of Hiba Bil Ewaz from Somedonnessa. The daughters of predeceased Abdus Sattar gifted their saham to the plaintiff respondent No.1 herein and also to defendant opposite party Nos. 2 and 3. In this way, the plain-tiff/petitioner became the co-sharer tenant in the case jote by way of inheritance; that the defendants/opposite parties having full knowledge about the same created the so called ewaz (exchange) deed dated 18.1.2000 in order to frustrate the right of pre-emption of the plaintiff and as such, the plaintiff/pre-emptor(respondent No.1, of both the civil petitions), instituted the suit for declaration to the effect that the deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 is actually a deed of sale and therefore, he has a right of pre-emption of .67 acre of land which was transferred by the said so called deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 to defendant No.1 by defendant No.2. 

 5. Defendant No.1 who is also pre-emptee opposite party No.1 contested the suit as well as the pre-emption case by filing written statement and written objection denying all material averments made in the plaint as well as in the application for pre-emption. Her contention inter alia is that admittedly the suit land along with other lands belonged to Abdul Gani Siddique and his wife Somedonnessa and it is also admitted that their two sons, Abdus Sattar and Abdul Majid died earlier. The defendant although admits the wasiatnama dated 7.4.1960 executed by Somedonnessa after the death of her husband Abdul Gani Siddique, but she claims that the plaintiff, who is son of late Abdus Sattar, one of the predeceased sons of Abdul Gani Siddique, did not get any property by the said wasiatnama and as such he is not a co-sharer tenant in the case jote by inheritance because Abdus Sattar died earlier to the owners of the jote. It is contended that admittedly Abdul Gani Siddique died leaving behind Somedunnessa, his wife, 2 sons and one daughter to inherit the properties left behind by him. Monir Hossain and Abdul Latif, two living sons of Somedonnessa, transferred the suit land along with other lands to Mojibar Rahman, who, then sold the same to his wife Mahmuda by a deed of sale. Mofizur Rahman, son of Majibar Rahman and Mahmuda gifted .47 acre of land and .20 acre of land respectively to the defendant No.2 by two gift deeds both dated 30.01.1995. The suit land described in the first schedule to the plaint measuring .67 acre of land was not fertile land, there was a homestead in plot No.88. That by earth filling all the lands of suit Plot Nos. 86, 87 and 88 have been developed. The land of Plot No. 116 is fertile land. The value of both the lands being the same the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, for the purpose of smooth cultivation, executed and registered the ewaz deed dated 18.1.2000 and thereafter on 19.1.2000 the defendant No.2 took possession and started cultivating paddy through bargadar. The said defendant also upon taking possession of .67 acre of land of Plot No.88 filled up .32 acre of land by earth and constructed house thereon and is possessing .34 acre of land of Plot No. 86 to 87 by cultivation. Thereafter, the defendant No.2 sold .34 acre of land of Plot No. 116 to defendant No.1 by registered deed of sale dated 23.5.2000. In this way, the defendant No.1 became the owner and possessor of 1.01 acres of land by the aforesaid two deeds. Since the alleged deed is a deed of exchange the plaintiff petitioner has no right to pre-empt the same and as such both the cases should be dismissed. 

 14. The trial Court on perusal of the said wasiatnama (Exhibit-2) found that the executrix, Somedonnessa, mentioned in the body of the said wasiatnama that since her son Abdus Sattar died earlier, the son and daughter of Abdus Sattar (her grandson and granddaughter) would get .73 acre of land. Such statement has been proved by the corroborative evidence of P.Ws. 2, 3 and OPWs (DWs)-1 and 2 and as such, the trial Court held "the plaintiff appears to be a co-sharer tenant in the case jote by inheritance". It further held "the Ewaz Deed dated 18.1.2000 is an out and out a sale deed". Relying upon the principle laid down in the case of Shafi Than Vs. Mannujan Hossain wife of A.Z.M. Delwar Hossain, Advocate and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 226 and also in the case of Alfazuddin Mollah and others Vs. Md. Almas Chokder and another reported in 56 DLR (AD) 179 and considering the evidence of O.P.Ws (D.Ws). 1 to 3 the trial Court thus held that "the plaintiff is entitled to get pre-emption over the case land as a co sharer-tenant in the case jote and the alleged deed of ewaz is actually a deed of sale".
